body:
> Attogram: Give me a little history of the teams, you know, location, how good they are.

Kimi:

Here's a quick side-by-side:

AFC Bournemouth — The South Coast Underdog
- Where: Bournemouth, a seaside town on England's south coast in Dorset.
- Ground: Dean Court, known as the Vitality Stadium — capacity around 11,300, historically the smallest ground in Premier League history.  The club just bought it back and is currently expanding it to roughly 20,000 seats. 
- History: Founded in 1899 (originally as Boscombe). They spent most of their existence in the lower leagues before a fairy-tale rise under Eddie Howe got them into the Premier League for the first time in 2015. They're the classic overachiever — a small club with a tiny budget that yo-yos between the Championship and the Premier League.
- How good? Solidly mid-to-lower Premier League. Right now they're sitting 13th in the table. 

Everton — The Historic Liverpool Giant
- Where: Liverpool, in England's northwest. They're the older, bigger club across town from Liverpool FC.
- Ground: The brand-new Hill Dickinson Stadium at Bramley-Moore Dock, opened in February 2025. It holds about 52,800 and cost roughly £750 million, replacing their iconic old home, Goodison Park, after 133 years.  
- History: Founded in 1878, one of the Football League's founder members. They've won 9 league titles and 5 FA Cups and were part of England's original "Big Five." Their heyday was the 1980s, but they haven't won a major trophy since 1995, which is a sore point for fans.
- How good? Historically massive, but they've been mid-table strugglers for much of the last decade. This season, though, they seem to have turned a corner — they're currently 6th in the Premier League. 

The vibe of this match: It's a classic "little guy vs. sleeping giant" fixture. Bournemouth are ahead 1-0 late in the game, which fits their scrappy, punch-above-their-weight identity. Everton, with their shiny new stadium and renewed ambition, will be frustrated if they can't find an equalizer.
